examples.text: カット！もう一度お願いしまーす。
examples.trans: Cut! Let's take it one more time, please.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Very common colloquial pronunciation/variant of すみません.

examples.text: すいません、ちょっと通してください。
examples.trans: Excuse me, please let me through.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: 分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

examples.text: いいの、初々しくてすごいかわいかったよ。こういう場所でのセックスは気分が乗らない？
examples.trans: It's totally fine—you looked fresh and super cute. Does filming in a place like this make it hard to get in the mood?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 私結構な潔癖症で、セックスはきれいなシーツの上じゃないと安心できないんです。
examples.trans: I'm actually quite particular about cleanliness, so I can't feel at ease unless we're on clean sheets.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Contracts では; launches a decision ('well then') or opens casual farewell じゃあね.

examples.text: じゃあシーン変更します。あとで真っ白なシーツでの絡み撮りますから、ここはキスシーンのみで。
examples.trans: All right, we're changing the scene! Later we'll shoot on pure white sheets, so we'll only do the kissing scene here.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Literary noun; 真の + noun means 'true/genuine'.

examples.text: 真の自由を求めて旅に出た。
examples.trans: He set out on a journey seeking true freedom.

examples.text: 今着てらっしゃるのがお似合いです。白はイノセンスの象徴ですから。
examples.trans: What you're wearing right now suits you best. White is the symbol of innocence.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 五日で十五本撮りって新記録っすよね。
examples.trans: Shooting fifteen videos in five days has got to be a new record.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Points to the place where the speaker currently stands.

examples.text: ここに座ってください。

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: でもうちは個性で勝負だ、個性で。
examples.trans: Still, our studio competes through originality.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; 時間が過ぎる means 'time passes / it's past the time'.

examples.text: 約束の時間が過ぎています。
examples.trans: We are past the appointment time.

examples.text: 夏休みがすぐに過ぎました。
俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Modifies nouns directly, as in 新しい店 ('new store') and 新しい仕事 ('new job').

examples.text: 新しい仕事が始まりました。
新しい靴を買いました。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
